logic.note: The serial protocol of the DFPlayer Mini manual: 10-byte frames with the 16-bit checksum (and the 8-byte form without it), play track 0x03, folder 0x0F, mp3 folder 0x12, next / previous, volume 0x06 / up / down, pause 0x0E, resume 0x0D, stop 0x16, reset 0x0C, sleep, queries 0x42 / 0x43 / 0x48 / 0x4C; replies 0x3F online, 0x41 ACK when FEEDBACK is 1, 0x3D track finished. Commands sent during the ~1 s start-up are ignored, as on the module. Malformed frames are dropped and reported. EQ, loop, source and advert commands are accepted without effect; ADKEY and IO buttons are not emulated.

timing.note: Bit-exact UART at 9600 baud both ways on the board's pins. A clip's length is estimated from its words (2.6 words per second plus 0.3 s), not from a real MP3; start-up is a typical 1 s and replies come after 20 ms.

analog.note: SPK_1-SPK_2 are a bridged source of up to 2 V RMS (0.5 W into 8 Ω at volume 30 on 5 V), scaled by volume and by VCC below 5 V; DAC_L / DAC_R give 0.7 V RMS through 1 kΩ. Levels are RMS values solved as DC: no waveform, no clipping, no hiss.

power.note: 20 mA idle plus the speaker's power at 80 % efficiency; on at 3.0 V, quieter below 3.2 V. Current peaks that reset the module on a weak supply are not modelled.

emulates: What the firmware sends and reads over serial, including the online / ACK / finished replies a library waits for
BUSY LOW while a clip plays
What each clip says, as text from the clips table: the speech bubble, read_speech and the {"said": …} test step
Whether a speaker is wired (no current on SPK_1 / SPK_2 or DAC: nobody hears it)
Start-up time, ignored early commands, wrong baud rate, bad checksums
doesNotEmulate: The real recorded voice: the browser speaks the words with its own text-to-speech voice
MP3 decoding, file order on the FAT32 card (0x03 plays the Nth file copied; 0x12 plays /mp3/NNNN.mp3 by name)
ADKEY resistor keys, IO_1 / IO_2 buttons, USB card-reader mode
Audio quality, hiss from a missing 1 kΩ on RX, pops at power-up
testOnRealDevice: Make the MP3s with sd-card/make-clips.sh (export_manufacturing), copy them to a FAT32 microSD as /mp3/0001.mp3, 0002.mp3 … and check every clip plays
Listen at the volume you set: small speakers distort above volume ~25 on 5 V
Put 1 kΩ in series with RX; without it some modules hiss or ignore commands
Power: on a battery the module can reset on loud clips; add 100 µF across VCC-GND
Clone modules (MH2024K, GD3200B chips) differ slightly: some need checksums, some need a longer start-up delay
